answer: Each identity stakes a bond whose signing key sits in a hardware root, so one machine cannot mint a thousand keys without a thousand physical modules. At dawn the stake becomes a vesting stream that releases only as the agent submits fresh nonces, each nonce hashing into the agent's pigment and advancing the release curve. Reusing an ember of an old stream voids the remaining balance. A farm needs real hardware and months of locked capital; the trade-off is slow onboarding for honest newcomers.
